title: Anunnaki–Elohim identity
statement: The Mesopotamian Anunnaki and the Elohim refer to the same underlying civilization, remembered through different languages and cultural records.

includes: Comparison of selected creation, council, labor, conflict, warning, and flood structures
excludes: Automatic one-to-one identity among every named deity
A stable Anunnaki or Elohim roster across all periods and texts
Zecharia Sitchin's Nibiru, orbit, gold-mining, or genetic chronology
Identity established by a popular etymology

source_references.locator: TBWTT-1:53; TBWTT-2:5 (defines the Elohim side of the comparison only)
s.v. Anuna (Anunnakku) p. 34; s.v. Igigu p. 103; underworld count p. 179

alternatives.statement: Anunnaki and Elohim name distinct divine collectives within different traditions.
Shared features reflect ancient Near Eastern literary inheritance or borrowing without literal shared beings.
Shared features are typological products of creation, divine-council, and flood narrative functions.
The apparent convergence results from selecting congenial elements from internally diverse corpora.
The Raëlian framework supplies the identity mapping rather than the ancient texts themselves.

revision_triggers: The collective-level proposition proves unstable across Mesopotamian or biblical periods and texts.
Source-language review materially changes a comparison currently treated as an observation.
A structured comparison supports only narrower motif, episode, or dependency relationships.
The dependency on claim woh-claim-0001 changes.
Public prose adds individual mappings or Sitchin-derived mechanisms not present in this record.
